facts.text: Flowers are the parts many plants use to make seeds.
Pollen is a fine powder made by flowers and other seed plants.
A flower's anther makes pollen, and the sticky stigma can catch pollen.
Many flowers have bright colors or sweet smells that help animals find them.
Bees visit flowers to drink nectar, a sweet liquid made by flowers.
Bees use nectar as an energy food that helps power their flying bodies.
Bees also collect pollen, which gives protein and other nutrients to young bees.
Some bees have special pollen baskets on their back legs to carry pollen home.
Pollination happens when pollen moves from one flower part to another flower part.
When a bee climbs into a flower, pollen can stick to its hairy body.
When the bee visits another flower, some pollen can rub off onto the new flower.
Wind, water, birds, bats, butterflies, and other insects can also move pollen.
Most animal pollinators are looking for food, not trying to help the flower on purpose.
After pollen lands in the right place, the flower may begin making seeds.
In flowering plants, seeds can grow inside a fruit.
Good pollination helps many plants make full, healthy fruit.
Seeds can grow into new plants when they land in a good place.
Some fruits that people eat begin as flowers that needed pollination.
Bees get food from flowers, and flowers can get help making seeds.
Many flowering plants need pollinators to help them make seeds and fruit.
Bees are important pollinators for wild plants, garden plants, and farm crops.
Flowers can feed bees through spring, summer, and fall when different plants bloom at different times.
Pollinators help many fruits and vegetables grow.
Bees and other pollinators can help make larger, more flavorful fruits on some crops.
More than 150 food crops in the United States depend on pollinators.
Pollinators are linked to about one out of every three bites of food people eat.
People can help bees by planting many kinds of flowers that bloom at different times.
Native plants can be good for native pollinators because they are used to the same place.
Using fewer pesticides can help keep bees and other pollinators safer.
Pollinator populations are declining in many places, so good habitat matters.
